title: On the Token Value Inequality in Efficient Reasoning
claim: Reasoning tokens contribute unequally; identifying core tokens lets efficient training compress redundant ones and improve the accuracy-token Pareto frontier.
layout: 2 panels, left analysis and right method, shared path diagram below with inset plot
description: A wide figure split into two shaded panels. The left, orange panel is titled 'Analysis: TokenProbe as a Core-Token Proxy'. It lists two numbered findings in bullets: token value inequality, and TokenProbe as a proxy that identifies core tokens (a yellow circle). The right, green panel is titled 'Methodology: Efficient GRPO'. It holds an inset scatter plot of performance (30–70) against tokens (2K–5K) with colored markers: ours (red circle) is top-left, and Grok, Gemini and Kimi sit elsewhere. Below, both panels share a path diagram running from Question to Answer. Colored curves show a fatal deviation path ending in a red X, a circular deadlock path (a purple tangle), a tortuous convergence path (blue), and a direct green path. Yellow dashed lines through dots mark hidden core tokens. A legend sits at the bottom, and a token budget triangle appears at upper right.
caption: Overview of TokenProbe: from token value inequality analysis \S[ref] to efficient reasoning \S[ref]. (a) Probing analysis shows that token contributions are highly unequal, and TokenProbe serves as an proxy for identifying core tokens. (b) Building on this insight, efficient GRPO improves it by preserving hidden core tokens, yielding better reasoning efficiency and Pareto performance.
abstract: Chain-of-Thought reasoning has enabled large language models to achieve substantial performance gains on complex tasks. However, these gains come at the cost of dramatically increased token consumption. This raises a fundamental question: is every token in the reasoning trace equally valuable? We present a diagnostic and optimization framework grounded in a key empirical finding: the value of tokens within a CoT reasoning sequence is highly non-uniform, and this non-uniformity can be effectively characterized by token-level log probability signals. We show that normalized log probability helps distinguish core tokens, which carry structural and decisive reasoning content, from redundant tokens, which are exploratory, low-confidence filler that contributes less directly to the final answer. Building on these findings, we formulate the TokenProbe framework around two empirical findings and one claim: findings identify token value inequality first and then establish TokenProbe as a core-token proxy, and the claim introduces an efficient GRPO objective positing that selectively compressing redundant tokens can yield Pareto improvements in the accuracy-token efficiency space. Empirically, our method preserves reasoning quality while reducing the token usage by 76% of the baseline. Under matched reasoning-length budgets, we show that it can even outperform strong flagship baselines like Gemini-3.1-Pro. Homepage: https://runjia.tech/tokenprobe/.
